note: Single source of truth for the pi-web merge boundary. `driftedUpstreamFiles` lists files agegr/pi-web owns that this fork has also edited — every one is a potential merge conflict, and a potential SILENT semantic conflict when git merges cleanly but the two sides changed different things. The automated sync (.github/workflows/component-updates.yml) intersects each incoming upstream release with this map to decide whether it may push to main unattended. Human-facing rationale lives in docs/ownership-boundaries.md.

riskModel.note: Risk follows STRUCTURAL drift, not total drift. Replacing an upstream inline style object with a className produces a large diff, but an upstream edit to the same line conflicts textually and fails the sync loudly — that is safe. Rewritten JSX trees and code moved across files are what merge cleanly while being wrong. components/ModelsConfig.tsx is the reference: 146 changed lines, only 12 structural, correctly rated low. Recompute with the hunk classifier described in docs/ownership-boundaries.md after any significant change to a shared file.

autoPushPolicy.note: Risk levels that force the sync to open a reviewed PR instead of pushing straight to main and triggering a signed release. Most upstream releases will land here, because the remaining drift is accepted by decision rather than pending cleanup — see `dispositions` and `decisionLog`. Narrow this list only if the drift itself actually goes away.

components/SessionSidebar.tsx.reason: ~500 lines were MOVED OUT into components/ProjectPicker.tsx and components/path-ui.tsx, which do not exist upstream. git merge does not track cross-file moves: an upstream edit to the project-picker block can merge back cleanly and silently resurrect a second copy.

components/AppShell.tsx.reason: Top-bar redesign (toolbar consolidated into a more-menu, inline styles to classNames) plus the mount point for desktop chrome. The desktop-only parts moved to components/desktop/; the remaining 376 structural lines are the fork's own interaction design, not desktop plumbing, so this file stays high risk by design rather than by neglect.

components/FileViewer.tsx.reason: Adds FileViewerToolbar and FileViewerStatus, file icons, a live-sync indicator and a retry action. Both components are defined inside FileViewer.tsx rather than moved out, so there is no cross-file resurrection risk — only a large diff. Kept deliberately.

components/FileExplorer.tsx.reason: Adds selection highlighting (selectedPath/onSelectPath) and moves git status colours onto CSS variables. Generic improvement, no desktop coupling. Kept deliberately.

components/ModelsConfig.tsx.reason: Already the correct shape: upstream inline style objects swapped for native-* classNames, 14 structural lines out of 148. Conflicts here are textual and trivially resolvable. Use this file as the model for restyling a shared component.

components/TabBar.tsx.reason: Accessibility work: role="tab", aria-selected, roving tabIndex, arrow-key navigation, Enter/Space activation, plus an empty state. A generic improvement with no desktop coupling, so it cannot be extracted anywhere — the only ways to remove this drift are upstreaming it or deleting the accessibility support. Kept deliberately.

components/ChatWindow.tsx.reason: Branding copy, the ChatMinimap mount and a redesigned empty state. Part of the fork's interaction design. Kept deliberately.

hooks/useTheme.ts.reason: Follows the OS colour scheme until the user picks a theme explicitly, and drops the ToggleOrigin argument so the view transition always starts from the centre. The view transition itself is unchanged from upstream. Kept deliberately.

components/PluginsConfig.tsx.reason: Already the correct shape: 6 structural lines out of 54, the rest is style-to-className substitution. Nothing to revert.

components/ChatInput.tsx.reason: Composer chrome restyle. Upstream changed this file in v0.8.1, and components/ChatInput.test.mjs covers it.

components/SkillsConfig.tsx.reason: Already the correct shape: 3 structural lines out of 44, the rest is style-to-className substitution. Nothing to revert.

lib/i18n/registry.ts.reason: Relative imports of ./messages/en and ./messages/zh-CN carry explicit .ts extensions so lib/i18n/registry.test.mjs can load the file through Node's native type stripping (same constraint that put allowImportingTsExtensions in tsconfig.json). Two import lines; conflicts here would be textual.

next.config.ts.reason: Desktop standalone build branch. Also holds serverExternalPackages, which upstream updates whenever it adds a pi package — do NOT auto-derive that list here.

app/layout.tsx.reason: native-theme.css import, branding title, dark-mode bootstrap script.

components/ChatMinimap.tsx.reason: className hooks only, no structural change — the intended shape for every restyled file.

eslint.config.mjs.reason: Adds ignores for the desktop build output directories.

lib/rpc-manager.ts.reason: Small fork edit in a file upstream changes often; watch it despite the low drift count.

components/FileIcons.tsx.reason: Adds an icon size parameter, consumed by the fork's FileViewer toolbar.

components/BranchNavigator.tsx.reason: className hook only, no structural change — the intended shape for every restyled file.

package.json.reason: Desktop scripts and Tauri deps. Name stays @agegr/pi-web on purpose — see docs/ownership-boundaries.md.

tsconfig.json.reason: resolveJsonModule for branding, plus allowImportingTsExtensions: lib/*.test.mjs load .ts sources through Node's native type stripping, which requires explicit extensions on relative imports.

.gitignore.reason: Desktop build output plus local agent tooling state (.claude/, .spec-workflow/).

README.md.reason: Fork-specific product docs, English and the language switcher's default entry point. Conflicts here are noisy but harmless — resolve by keeping the fork version.

README.zh-CN.md.reason: Fork-specific product docs, Simplified Chinese translation of README.md. Same handling as README.md. Upstream's other translations (ja, ru) are deleted in this fork on purpose — if a sync resurrects them, delete them again rather than translating Pi Agent docs into a language nobody here maintains.

lib/file-access.ts.reason: Routes homedir() through userHome() so Next's file tracer stops folding it into a build-time glob of the whole user profile — the walk that made every Windows build fail. One import plus call swaps; conflicts here would be textual.

dispositions.accepted: Reviewed and kept. The drift is either the fork's own interaction design or a generic improvement with no desktop coupling, so it cannot be extracted into components/desktop/. Removing it would mean deleting a feature. These files stay permanent review points; that is the running cost of a UI fork, not a backlog item. Do not reopen without new information.
dispositions.reduce: Drift that can be removed without losing anything — desktop-only code that belongs in components/desktop/, or fork additions sitting in an upstream file that can move to a fork-owned one. Act on these.

decisionLog: 2026-07-26 — lib/api-types.ts: fork update types moved to lib/app-update-types.ts; file now matches upstream and left the manifest.

2026-07-26 — TabBar, FileExplorer, useTheme, FileViewer: assessed as generic improvements with zero desktop coupling. Upstreaming was declined, so accepted rather than reverted — reverting would delete working features to save CI review time.

2026-07-26 — lib/file-access.ts and app/api/default-cwd/route.ts: a literal homedir() in readdirSync/join arguments made @vercel/nft glob the whole user profile at build time, which is why the Windows release leg never succeeded. Routed both through defaultCwdBase(); accepted as new drift in two upstream files.

2026-07-26 — lib/user-home.ts added; five upstream files now call userHome() instead of homedir(). A literal homedir() reaching an fs call made @vercel/nft glob the entire user profile at build time. lib/directory-browser.ts (added upstream in v0.8.1) was the source of the fatal <home>/**/* walk, which is why Windows releases started failing exactly when v0.8.1 merged.
